title: How the Internet Finds a Website

scenes.narration: You type a website name into your browser. But how does your computer know where that website lives?
scenes.caption: You enter a website address

scenes.narration: First, your browser asks a directory system called DNS to find the website's numerical address.
scenes.caption: DNS looks up the address

scenes.narration: The request travels across networks, passing through routers that guide it toward the right server.
scenes.caption: Routers guide the request

scenes.narration: The server receives the request and sends the website files back across the network.
scenes.caption: The server sends the page

scenes.narration: Your browser assembles those files into the page you see on your screen.
scenes.caption: Your browser builds the page

scenes.narration: All of this happens in seconds, every time you visit a website.
scenes.caption: A journey completed in seconds
